''' Harald Rose ''' (born 14 February 1935; died 27 July 2026) was a German [[physicist]]. He was a laureate of the 2011 [[Wolf Prize in Physics]] and the 2020 [[Kavli Prize]] in Nanoscience for the development of [[aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy]].

== Biography ==
Rose was born in [[Bremen]].<ref>Kürschners of German scholar calendars 2009 {{in lang|de}}</ref>

Rose received in 1964 his physics [[Diplom]] in theoretical [[electron optics]] under [[Otto Scherzer]] at the [[Technical University of Darmstadt|Technische Universität Darmstadt]]. From 1976 to 1980 he was principal research scientist at [[New York State Department of Health]]. In 1973–1974 he spent one research year at the [[Enrico Fermi Institute]] of the  [[University of Chicago]] and in 1995–1996 one research year at [[Cornell University]] and the [[University of Maryland]]. From 1980 to his retirement in 2000 as professor emeritus, he was active at the University of Darmstadt in the Physics Department. Since 2009 he has held a [[Carl Zeiss AG|Carl Zeiss]] funded Senior Professorship at the [[University of Ulm]].<ref name="Universität Ulm 2016">{{cite web | title=Carl-Zeiss-Stiftungsprofessur | website=Universität Ulm | date=8 August 2016 | url=https://www.uni-ulm.de/universitaet/hochschulkommunikation/presse-und-oeffentlichkeitsarbeit/aktuelles-thema/carl-zeiss-stiftungsprofessur/ | language=de | access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref> Rose has 105 patents of scientific instruments and electrooptical components. He died on July 26, 2026.<ref>[https://www.vrm-trauer.de/traueranzeige/harald-rose Vrm-trauer.de: Harald Rose] (german)</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* 1987 Honorary Professor of the [[Xi'an Jiaotong University]], China<ref name="Honda Global 2008" />
* 2003 Distinguished Scientist Award of the [[Microscopy Society of America]]<ref name="Microscopy Society of America">{{cite web | title=News | website=Microscopy Society of America | url=https://www.microscopy.org/news/news_0321.cfm | access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref>
* 2006 Karl Heinz Beckurts Prize (together with [[Maximilian Haider]] and [[Knut Urban]])<ref name="pro-physik.de 2021">{{cite web | title=Kavli-Preis 2020 für Arbeiten zur Elektronenmikroskopie | website=pro-physik.de | date=14 December 2021 | url=https://www.pro-physik.de/nachrichten/kavli-preis-2020-fuer-arbeiten-zur-elektronenmikroskopie | language=de | access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref>
* 2008 Honda Prize (together with Maximilian Haider and Knut Urban)<ref name="pro-physik.de 2021" /><ref name="Honda Global 2008">{{cite web | title=September 30, 2008 Team of German Researchers to Receive Honda Prize 2008 for Their Achievement in Aberration-Corrected Transmission Electron Microscopy for High-Resolution Visualization of Atomic Structures | website=Honda Global | date=30 September 2008 | url=https://global.honda/newsroom/news/2008/c080930-eng.html | access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref>
* 2008 Honorary Fellow of the Royal Society of Microscopy (Hon FRMS)<ref name="RMS">{{cite web | title=Honorary Fellows | website=RMS | url=https://www.rms.org.uk/membership/honorary-fellows.html | access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref>
* 2009 Robert Wichard Pohl Prize<ref name="DPG 2019">{{cite web | title=Preisträgerinnen und Preisträger | website=DPG | date=17 December 2019 | url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/auszeichnungen/dpg-preise/robert-wichard-pohl-preis/preistraeger | language=de | access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref>
* 2011 [[Wolf Prize]] for Physics (together with Maximilian Haider and Knut Urban)<ref name="TU Darmstadt">{{cite web | title=Harald Rose | website=TU Darmstadt | url=https://www.tu-darmstadt.de/universitaet/mitten_in_der_gesellschaft/geschichte_persoenlichkeiten/persoenlichkeiten_1/harald_rose/index.en.jsp | access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref>
* 2013 [[BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award]] in Basic Sciences (together with Maximilian Haider and Knut Urban)<ref name="Premios Fronteras 2019">{{cite web | title=Harald Rose | website=Premios Fronteras | date=15 December 2019 | url=https://www.frontiersofknowledgeawards-fbbva.es/galardonados/harald-rose-2/ | access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref>
* 2020 [[Kavli Prize]] in Nanoscience (together with [[Maximilian Haider]] and [[Knut Urban]] and [[Ondrej Krivanek]]).<ref>[http://kavliprize.org/prizes-and-laureates/prizes/2020-kavli-prize-nanoscience 2020 Kavli Prize in Nanoscience], www.kavliprize.org. Retrieved 27 May 2020.</ref>
